chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Said from Ibn Abi Umayr from Jamil from Mihran said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the mukatab (a slave who has contracted for manumission upon paying a sum) who dies and leaves children. He said: 'If it was stipulated for him [that his children would remain slaves until the debt was paid], then his children are slaves. And if it was not stipulated for him, his children strive in their father's mukatabah and are freed when they pay [the debt].'

key_terms.اَلْمُكَاتَبِ: A slave who has contracted with his master to pay a specific sum for his manumission.
key_terms.مَمَالِيكُ: Plural of slave; here referring to the children remaining in slavery.
key_terms.مُكَاتَبَةِ أَبِيهِمْ: The manumission contract of their father.

ai.seo_question: What happens to the children of a mukatab slave when he dies?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the inheritance rules for a *mukatab* (slave with a manumission contract) who dies leaving offspring, a key issue in Shia fiqh regarding the continuity of servitude versus freedom. It establishes that the children's status depends on the specific stipulations of the contract: if the master required the children to remain slaves to pay the debt, they inherit the father's enslaved status; otherwise, they are entitled to secure their own freedom by paying the remaining balance. This ruling underscores the principle of contractual specificity in manumission agreements within Shia jurisprudence.
